cards.text: Back in Canaan, Joseph's father Jacob learns there's grain in Egypt, and his sons just stand there. Jacob says, "Why are you staring at one another?" Friend, that's every group chat right after somebody asks, "So who's paying?"

cards.question: Jacob tells his sons he's heard there's grain in Egypt. What does he want them to do?

answers.text: Buy grain so they can live
Ask Pharaoh for land to live on

cards.text: So the brothers head down to Egypt. Well, most of them. Jacob keeps one son back home.

cards.question: So ___ of Joseph's brothers go down to Egypt to buy grain.
Which of Joseph's brothers does Jacob keep at home?
Jacob keeps Benjamin home because he needs him to watch the flocks.

cards.text: Jacob's sons join the crowd heading to Egypt, because the famine has hit Canaan too. And the man selling grain to everybody? That's Joseph, the ruler of the land.

cards.question: When Joseph's brothers arrive in front of him, what do they do?

answers.text: Bow with their faces to the ground
Ask to speak with Pharaoh himself
Hand over the gifts from Jacob

cards.text: Joseph sees his brothers and recognizes them. They look RIGHT at him and don't recognize him at all, and friend, if I walked in, you'd know me by the mustache from across the room.

cards.question: Joseph treats his brothers as ___ and speaks ___ to them.

cards.text: Joseph remembers his dreams about them. Then he opens his mouth, and friend, it is NOT a welcome speech.

cards.question: What does Joseph accuse his brothers of being?

cards.text: The brothers say, "Not so, my lord." They're honest men, all sons of one man, here to buy food, but Joseph says they've come to see if the land is vulnerable.

cards.question: Trying to clear their names, the brothers tell Joseph they're ___ brothers, the sons of one man in Canaan.
The brothers tell Joseph their youngest brother is back home with their father.

cards.text: And the other missing brother? They say "one is no more." Friend, that's texting the group chat "Anybody heard from Mike?" while Mike is IN the group chat.
Joseph says, "Just as I said, you are spies!" Now he's going to test them.

cards.question: Joseph swears, "As surely as Pharaoh lives." What has to happen before the brothers can leave?

answers.text: They pay for their grain twice

cards.question: Joseph says one brother can go get the youngest while the rest stay locked up. Then he puts all of them in prison for ___ days.

cards.text: On the third day, Joseph tells them, "I fear God." Then he lays out a new deal.

cards.question: In Joseph's new deal, how many of the brothers stay behind in custody?
Under Joseph's new deal, the brothers who go home with grain must bring their youngest brother back to him.

cards.text: The brothers agree to it. Then, standing right there in front of Joseph, they start talking among themselves, and it gets heavy.

cards.question: The brothers say to one another, "Surely we are being punished." What do they say it's because of?

answers.text: What they did to their brother
How they spoke to the ruler
Coming to Egypt without a gift

cards.question: The brothers remember their brother pleading with them while they would not listen. Then one of them says, "Didn't I tell you not to sin against the boy?" Which brother?

cards.text: Reuben adds, "Now we must account for his blood!" Every family has that one sibling sitting on an "I told you so" for years, friend, and Reuben just cashed his in.

cards.question: The brothers know Joseph understands every word they're saying to one another.

cards.text: There's an interpreter between them, so they have no idea he's following along. And Joseph turns away from them and weeps.

cards.question: When Joseph turns back, he takes ___ from them and has him bound right before their eyes.

cards.text: Then Joseph gives orders to fill their bags with grain and give them provisions for the trip. And he adds one more order.

cards.question: Joseph orders each man's ___ put back in his sack.

cards.text: They load the grain on their donkeys and head out. Where they stop for the night, one brother opens his sack to feed his donkey, and there's his silver, right in the mouth of the sack.

cards.question: The brother tells the others his silver has been returned. How do they react?

answers.text: Their hearts sink and they tremble
They laugh and thank the ruler
They turn back to return it

cards.text: They turn to one another and say, "What is this that God has done to us?" And friend, they haven't even made it home yet.

Back in Canaan, the brothers tell their father Jacob everything that happened. The harsh lord of the land, the spy charge, and his deal: leave one brother, take the food home, and bring the youngest back.

cards.question: The brothers tell Jacob what the lord of the land promised if they bring their youngest brother back. What is it?

answers.text: Their brother back and the right to trade
Free grain for the rest of the famine
A place to live near the ruler himself

cards.text: Then they start emptying their sacks. Remember, one brother already found his silver where they stopped for the night.

cards.question: What turns up as the brothers empty their sacks?
When Jacob and his sons see all the bags of silver, they're relieved.

cards.text: Then Jacob speaks up: "You have deprived me of my sons."

cards.question: Jacob goes on: "___ is gone and ___ is no more."

cards.text: Then he says, "Now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is going against me!" Friend, I said the same thing my first week in the junk drawer, except I said it to a dead battery.

cards.question: Reuben makes his father an offer. What does Reuben say Jacob can do if he fails to bring Benjamin back?
Jacob agrees to put Benjamin in Reuben's care for the trip to Egypt.

cards.text: Jacob says Benjamin's brother is dead and he alone is left. If harm comes to him on the journey, "you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow."
And that's where we leave this family for now. Hang onto your apron, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Card 3 says 'Well, most of them. Jacob keeps one son back home.' Card 4 then asks how many of Joseph's brothers go. Joseph has eleven brothers, so if one stays home, 'eleven' is ruled out and the answer can be worked out by subtraction instead of reasoned from the moment.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 17 cites only Genesis 42:14, but 'Now he's going to test them' tells Genesis 42:15 ('And this is how you will be tested'). The citation should be Genesis 42:14-15.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'All but one of them' is false for the new deal, but it is true of Joseph's first plan in Genesis 42:16 ('Send one of your number to get your brother; the rest of you will be confined'). It is a true detail elsewhere in the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The joke says Reuben was 'sitting on an "I told you so" for years' and 'just cashed his in.' This presents Reuben as gloating, and states his motive as fact, at a moment of guilt and anguish that makes Joseph weep. It laughs at Reuben rather than with his situation.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: Card 1 cites Genesis 42:29-33, but 'and bring the youngest back' tells Genesis 42:34 ('But bring your youngest brother back to me'). The citation should be Genesis 42:29-34.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The two blanks can be swapped. 'Simeon is gone and Joseph is no more' is just as defensible, since the brothers already said of Joseph that 'one is no more' (Genesis 42:13). A baker could argue the reversed order is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new event from Papa Dorin's junk drawer days: during his first week, he said 'Everything is going against me!' to a dead battery. The docs only let jokes make up small moments around his bakery. They don't allow adding new events to his backstory.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.
